answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: require cross-attestation from unrelated established identities before a withdrawal clears, because cedar only stays cheap while a closed ring of clones cannot assemble independent attestations without hiring real ones. Concretely, nebula is enforced in the ledger: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any nadir approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
